text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Unity is the message of the elections in the (right wing) Democratic Rally Party. Nicos Anastassiades wins the party leadership, polling 69 percent of the vote compared to 31 percent gained by runner-up Demetris Syllouris.
- Britain's envoy on the Cyprus dispute Sir David Hannay says there is common ground in the positions of the two sides, but he will not reveal it.
- The people of Cyprus will not vote for (current president) Glafcos Clerides in the presidential elections of 1998, says Demetris Christofias, leader of the communist Akel party.
- Yiannis Katsourides, a founding member of Akel, dies.

- David Hannay makes a clear attempt at improving the already negative climate for the direct talks scheduled between the Greek and the Turkish Cypriot sides next month by stating that there is common ground in their positions.

- A bicommunal football match scheduled to take place this week has been called off after the Turkish Cypriot side backtracked on an initial understanding on the vetting of 300 Greek Cypriot fans going to the occupied areas to watch the game.
- Nicos Anastassiades wins the elections in Disy. Outgoing president Yiannakis Matsis states he will be present to offer his services to the party leadership.
